history.summary: One of the 108 Divya Desams, glorified in the Divya Prabandha by the Azhwar saints (6th-9th centuries) and mentioned in Sangam literature (3rd century works like Madurai Kanchi, Kaliththokai, Paripadal), indicating an antiquity of over 2,000 years. Founded by the Pandyas; the pillared halls and major shrines were added by Vijayanagara and Madurai Nayak kings in the 16th century. It is famed for its rare Ashtanga Vimana showing Vishnu in three postures — seated (ground floor), standing as Sri Suryanarayana (first floor), and reclining in Ananthasayana (second floor). It is where Periyalvar (Vishnucitta) composed the Thirupallandu after establishing Vishnu's supremacy in the Pandya court. Legend says the Lord appeared to slay the demon Somuka who had abducted the Vedas.

name: Koodal Azhagar Temple
town_description: Ancient temple city on the Vaigai river in southern Tamil Nadu, among the oldest continuously inhabited cities of India; the Koodal Azhagar temple stands near the Periyar bus stand in central Madurai, close to the Meenakshi temple.

travel.road: Central Madurai near Periyar Bus Stand; reached by city bus, auto or taxi; roadside parking (fee)

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Vaikasi Brahmotsavam and the float festival are the highlights
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:30 AM – 12:00 PM, 4:00 PM – 9:00 PM (verify: some sources give 6:00 AM – 12:00 PM / 4:00 – 8:00 PM; Viswaroopa darshan at 6:00 AM)
